30.0.s.en: 1. A warning against trusting in Pharaoh:

30.0.0.en: 1 "Woe to the rebellious children," saith the LORD, "that carry out a plan, but not of me; and that pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: 2 That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt! 3 Therefore shall the strength of Pharaoh be your shame, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt your confusion. 4 For his princes were at Zoan, and his ambassadors came to Hanes. 5 They were all ashamed of a people that could not profit them, nor be an help nor profit, but a shame, and also a reproach." 6 The burden of the beasts of the south: into the land of trouble and anguish, from whence come the young and old lion, the viper and fiery flying serpent, they will carry their riches upon the shoulders of young asses, and their treasures upon the bunches of camels, to a people that shall not profit them. 7 For the Egyptians shall help in vain, and to no purpose: therefore have I called her Rahab who sits still.

30.0.1.en: "Woe to the rebellious children, saith the LORD, that carry out a plan, but not of me; and that pour out a libation, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: that walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt" [1-2].

30.0.2.en: Here, in the fourth woe, the following is observed:

30.0.3.en: A. He calls them rebellious children, because they rejected the counsel of God their Father and did not trust in Him, but counted Pharaoh as their father who would rescue them. Our sonship to God is not words or mere emotions, but a meeting with Him, a reliance upon Him, and an entering with Him into deep, practical relationships; this sonship condemns us if we do not walk as befits it.

30.0.4.en: B. They carried out a plan [1], that is, they took counsel among themselves and did not seek the counsel of God, nor did they ask His faithful men.

30.0.5.en: C. "Pour out a libation," or "cover with a covering, but not of my spirit" [1], meaning that they wanted to cover over their counsel and hide from me what they were doing (Isa 29:15-16), so they deprived themselves of the leading of my Holy Spirit.

30.0.6.en: D. "That they may add sin to sin" [1]. Thus they were sliding down a chain of sins, which began with rebellion against their heavenly Father, since they counted Him unable to protect them, then they took counsel while ignoring His counsel, then they tried to hide their actions, and so on...

30.1.0.en: E. "That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth" [2]; they sent messengers to Pharaoh to ally with him... They went down to Egypt, and did not accept God, who lifts them up to Himself; they accepted going down instead of going up, or descending instead of ascending toward the heavenly things.

30.1.1.en: The children of God do not accept descending and going down, as it were, to the love of the world (Egypt), but practice constant growth so as to ascend every day toward the heavenly life, saying: "Come, and let us go up to the mountain of the LORD" (Mic 4:2).

30.2.0.en: F. The fortress of Pharaoh is counted as shame to them, and the protection of Egypt as a shameful shadow [3]. Their messengers reached Zoan and Hanes seeking help and counsel, and they received shame and confusion.

30.2.1.en: Zoan was the capital of Upper Egypt, on the eastern bank of the Delta and on the Tanitic branch of the Nile; the kings fortified it and made it a capital to watch for attacks coming upon Egypt from the east. In this city the negotiations between Moses and Pharaoh took place (Ps 78:12, 43); the Assyrians occupied it afterward, and the Greeks called it "Tanis," and today it is called "San el-Hagar."

30.2.2.en: Hanes lies about 50 miles south of Memphis on the western bank of the Nile, and it is still known as Ehnasya, that is, Ahnasia, and in the Greco-Roman age it was known as Heracleopolis Magna.

30.3.0.en: The prophet likens the messengers coming from Judah to Egypt to Behemoth (the beasts of the south: [6]), meaning a kind of Egyptian crocodile, the hippopotamus. They came seeking help from a land full of hardships and distresses, unable to save itself, full of lions, vipers, and fiery flying serpents; they came carrying their goods on donkeys and camels as gifts to Pharaoh and his men, who were unable to protect them. They came for safety to a region of troubles and deadly dangers.

30.4.0.en: He calls Egypt by a poetic, symbolic name, "Rahab who sits still" [7]; "Rahab" is meant as "the broad," or "the wide," or "the great," or "the proud," for Egypt became proud and arrogant, making beautiful but unrealistic promises, and instead of rising to help the kingdom of Judah and support it, she "sat" watching Judah as it was carried off captive to Babylon.

30.4.1.en: Thus the prophet Isaiah warns the kingdom of Judah, which was stricken with stupidity and blindness when it resorted to proud Egypt seeking her protection.

30.5.s.en: 2. Disciplines because of despising the commandment of the Lord:

30.5.0.en: 8 Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever: 9 That this is a rebellious people, lying children, children that will not hear the law of the LORD: 10 Which say to the seers, See not; and to the beholders, Behold not for us right things, speak unto us smooth things, behold deceits: 11 Get you out of the way, turn aside out of the path, cause the Holy One of Israel to cease from before us. 12 Wherefore thus saith the Holy One of Israel, Because ye despise this word, and trust in oppression and perverseness, and stay thereon: 13 Therefore this iniquity shall be to you as a breach ready to fall, swelling out in a high wall, whose breaking cometh suddenly at an instant. 14 And he shall break it as the breaking of the potters' vessel that is broken in pieces; he shall not spare: so that there shall not be found in the bursting of it a sherd to take fire from the hearth, or to take water withal out of the pit. 15 For thus saith the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength: and ye would not. 16 But ye said, No; for we will flee upon horses; therefore shall ye flee: and, We will ride upon the swift; therefore shall they that pursue you be swift. 17 One thousand shall flee at the rebuke of one; at the rebuke of five shall ye flee: till ye be left as a beacon upon the top of a mountain, and as an ensign on an hill.

30.5.1.en: God asked the prophet Isaiah to write a warning to the people of Judah on a large tablet that all could see in a public place, and also to record it in a book so that it might remain forever [8]. Perhaps he wrote on the tablet "Rahab who sits still" to warn them against trusting in Pharaoh (Egypt), who sits watching, while in the book were written the sins of Judah and the prophecies and visions that God gave him.

30.6.0.en: The chief sin of Judah is that they are a rebellious people who reject the law of the Lord and accept the words of the false prophets. The Law was bitter and harsh to them, because it exposes their sins and demands of them the narrow divine way; therefore they told the prophets, the seers, not to see and not to behold right things, but sought the deceitful words of the false prophets, which he calls here "smooth things" and "deceits" [10], which give the soul a temporary tranquility through ignoring sin and calming consciences. By this they rejected the prophets' standing in their way, and asked that the Holy One of Israel be removed from before them [11].

30.7.0.en: As for the fruits of disobedience and of rejecting the true prophets and the Holy One of Israel, they are that they became like a high wall that cracks and falls and is shattered in a moment [13], and are likened to a potter's vessel that falls and is crushed completely without pity, so that no part of it is left fit to be used for taking fire from a hearth or water from a pit... Thus it is good for nothing at all except to be gathered and cast into a dunghill...

30.8.0.en: The prophet portrays the destruction of the kingdom of Judah because they rejected the counsel of the Lord who says: "In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength" [15]; that is, the secret of your salvation is in your repentance and your return to God with stillness and calm in confidence; this is the true strength. But they refused repentance with faith in God, for they said: "No; for we will flee upon horses... therefore shall they that pursue you be swift" [16], that is, they relied on human resources, especially the horses and chariots of Egypt, and thought that they were able to save them quickly, but the enemy pursues them with greater speed and overtakes them. Even more bitter, they flee before nothing, for one soldier of the enemies terrifies a thousand men of the sons of Judah, and five soldiers terrify the whole army of Judah; they leave their weapons and flee in humiliation, to become like a lone tree or a beacon on a mountain, or a banner or a sign on a hill; they become a lesson for all generations.

30.8.1.en: When King Hezekiah returned to God (2 Kgs 20) and turned toward the wall while on his deathbed, he lifted his mind to heaven and overcame death victoriously.

30.9.s.en: 3. The mercies of God toward His repentant people:

30.9.0.en: 18 And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he rise up, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of truth: blessed are all they that wait for him. 19 For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem: thou shalt weep no more: he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee. 20 And the Lord shall give you bread in distress and water in affliction; thy teachers shall not hide themselves any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: 21 And thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left. 22 Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence. 23 Then shall he give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures. 24 The oxen likewise and the young asses that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan. 25 And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers and streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall. 26 Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound.

30.9.1.en: "And therefore will the LORD wait, that he may be gracious unto you, and therefore will he rise up, that he may have mercy upon you: for the LORD is a God of truth: blessed are all they that wait for him" [8].

30.9.2.en: The prophet Isaiah expects them to return to God and abandon their reliance on the human arm, waiting for the Lord as their Savior; but strangely it is not Isaiah who waits for this, but the Lord Himself, who takes the initiative in love, waiting for their return, longing for them so that He may be gracious to them and have mercy upon them as a God of truth who loves His creation. In His love He waits to pour out the abundance of His grace upon His prodigal son who returns to Him (Lk 15).

30.9.3.en: The Lord's waiting also means His coming plan for the salvation of many, which is centered on the following points:

30.10.0.en: A. The dwelling of His people in Jerusalem: "For the people shall dwell in Zion at Jerusalem" [19]; that is, He brings them into the Church of the New Testament, where is the peace of God which passeth all understanding ("Jerusalem" means "the place of peace").

30.10.1.en: Jerusalem also points to heaven, Jerusalem which is above, which is the mother of us all (Gal 4:26), as though our salvation lies in God's drawing His people to the heavenly life.

30.10.2.en: B. The removal of sorrow and weeping: "thou shalt weep no more" [19], since the Church is an image of heaven, in which there is no sorrow nor pain... (Rev 21:4). Here he does not mean outward weeping but the loss of inner joy... for the Church shares with her Bridegroom His sufferings, which are not separated from the joy of His resurrection. In other words, the Church is the Kingdom of Christ, which bears the mark of the Cross that is not separated from the Resurrection.

30.10.3.en: It is fitting for us here to distinguish between sorrow according to the will of God and despondency, or the loss of comfort and peace. Sorrow according to the will of God is a spiritual virtue accompanied by the comforts of God and His peace which passeth all understanding, while despondency is a vice that reveals a state of despair and lack of hope, which destroys the life and will of man. St. John Chrysostom says: [It attacks not only the body but also the soul itself... It is always deadly, draining the strength of the soul". He encouraged the deaconess Olympias to overcome despondency, as a tyrant that dampens the spirits.

30.10.4.en: C. A swift answer to prayers: "he will be very gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry; when he shall hear it, he will answer thee" [19]; He allows distress and affliction, but He hears the cries, so He gives bread and water and does not leave man in want [20].

30.11.0.en: D. If the Lord Himself becomes a teacher (Jn 2:23) and His Holy Spirit a leader and comforter for the Church, then one of the Lord's blessings is that He gives the spirit of sincere teaching and straight spiritual guidance without deviation, and a comforter for the Church, then one of the Lord's blessings is that He gives the spirit of sincere teaching and straight spiritual guidance without deviation; "thy teachers shall not hide themselves any more, but thine eyes shall see thy teachers: and thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it, when ye turn to the right hand, and when ye turn to the left" [21].

30.11.1.en: Teaching and knowledge are a gift from God Himself, who sanctifies the ear to hear His words and respond to them, and sanctifies the mind, the heart, and the feelings, so that man in his entirety becomes responsive to the will of God as declared through His word.

30.11.2.en: In this spirit the early Church lived believing that God alone is able to send laborers to His harvest, giving them His grace to speak the word of truth uprightly, and giving the hearers grace to respond to it and understand it.

30.11.3.en: This also is what moved the Fathers of the Church to persevere in prayers and through a holy life in order to enjoy the gift of divine knowledge.

30.11.4.en: * Let us urge God to give us, as the word grows in us, so that we may receive the riches of breadth of mind in Christ Jesus, and thus become able to hear the holy, sacred words.

30.11.5.en: * Many have sought to interpret the divine Scriptures... but not all have succeeded in that. For rarely is there found one who has this grace from God.

30.11.6.en: Origen Perhaps by the teachers hiding in the Church he means the company of the prophets, for with the coming of the Lord Christ, the unique Teacher, the prophecies are enlightened and the mysteries of the Old Testament, which points to salvation, are revealed, and it declares the person of the Messiah and His saving works and His divine role in the life of the Church.

30.12.0.en: E. The rejection of idolatrous worship with all its luxury: "Ye shall defile also the covering of thy graven images of silver, and the ornament of thy molten images of gold: thou shalt cast them away as a menstruous cloth; thou shalt say unto it, Get thee hence" [22].

30.12.1.en: Since most of the idols were of wood or pottery overlaid with silver or gold, the work of salvation is the exposure of the inside, for man receives by the Spirit of God the power to say to it "Get thee hence"; so it comes out from the outer covering that hides its reality, that it represents the cloth of the unclean menstruous woman, just as it comes out of the heart of the believer who receives the Lord of glory Jesus as sanctified to Him.

30.12.2.en: Our Christ bears sufferings outwardly, so that He seems to have "no form nor comeliness; and when we shall see him, there is no beauty that we should desire him" (Isa 53:2), but He gives us His inward glories that cannot be comprehended. As for the love of the world, it gives outward enticements, and inside them is stench and corruption.

30.13.0.en: F. The grace of rain: "Then shall he give the rain of thy seed, that thou shalt sow the ground withal; and bread of the increase of the earth, and it shall be fat and plenteous: in that day shall thy cattle feed in large pastures" [23].

30.13.1.en: The age of the Messiah in the minds of the prophets was "the age of rain" or "the age of abundant waters." We recall, for example, that this age was described as one in which God gives the rain in its season (Ezek 34:26), and the rain waters the earth so that it brings forth an abundance of grain and crops for man to eat and the beasts find rich pasture [23], and so on..., and there is no hunger or thirst (Isa 31:9; 49:10). Living waters flow out from the Temple and bring forth marvelous fruits and very many trees grow (Ezek 47:1-12); an open fountain comes forth for the house of David that cuts off the idols of the earth and removes the unclean spirit (Zech 13:1-2). The springs of Judah flow with water and a fountain comes forth from the house of the Lord that gives life (Joel 3:18; Zech 14:8), making glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the Most High (Ps 46:4).

30.13.2.en: In short, the Messianic age is linked with the holy waters, which give quenching of thirst and turn the wilderness into a fruitful land, water the believers like the trees of the paradise of God, remove uncleanness and cleanse the earth of idol worship, and offer life and sanctification... These holy waters are Baptism and the gift of the Holy Spirit.

30.13.3.en: * The first waters brought forth life; let no one wonder if the waters in Baptism can also give life.

30.13.4.en: Tertullian * You are outside Paradise, O catechumens; you share with Adam your first father in his exile, and now the door is opened (Baptism as a life in Paradise) and you return to where you came out.

30.14.0.en: St. Gregory of Nazianzus Thus souls are watered in the Messianic age just as bodies are satisfied, not through temporal pleasures but through their sanctification by the Lord, so that everything is good, blessed, and pure for them. "The oxen likewise and the young asses (a reference to the body) that ear the ground shall eat clean provender, which hath been winnowed with the shovel and with the fan" [24].

30.14.1.en: It was the custom to leave for the animals that work the land a fodder that is a mixture of straw with a few remains of grain, but in the Messianic age, when good things overflow, salted and winnowed food is offered to the body, that is, the straw and the dust and so on are removed from it, a sign of our care for the body as a good and sacred element for the sake of the Kingdom of God.

30.14.2.en: With the coming of the Word of God incarnate, our view of the body was sanctified; therefore the Apostle John forbade those who deny that Jesus came in the flesh (1 Jn 4:2; 2 Jn 7); and the early Church resisted the Gnostic thought which said that the body is an element of darkness that must be destroyed.

30.14.3.en: * The body is not the source of evil, but freedom of choice (free will).

30.14.4.en: * The body is the dwelling of the soul.

30.14.5.en: * The body is the instrument of the spirit... working in the company of the soul.

30.14.6.en: * The Word became flesh in order to change our body into spirit... and in order to sanctify the whole body with Him, since in Him the firstfruits were sanctified.

30.15.0.en: St. Gregory of Nyssa "And there shall be upon every high mountain, and upon every high hill, rivers and streams of waters in the day of the great slaughter, when the towers fall" [25]. It is as though even the high mountains and hills find sufficient water; perhaps this points to the rich grace of God, which overflows not only upon the simple and the common people but also draws kings, rulers, leaders, and nobles to faith, in the day in which those who deny the faith are slain spiritually, those who fell like towers. It was fitting for the Jewish leaders to be towers for the world, seeing the Kingdom of Christ and preaching it, but they became resisters of the truth and so collapsed, a matter that grieved the Apostle Paul.

30.16.0.en: G. Great illumination: "Moreover the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun, and the light of the sun shall be sevenfold, as the light of seven days, in the day that the LORD bindeth up the breach of his people, and healeth the stroke of their wound" [26].

30.16.1.en: As the Lord heals the wounds of the soul and the body, sanctifying man in his entirety, with all his powers of instincts, feelings, emotions, mind, and so on..., he bears the image of his Creator, "the true Light," and so becomes a light to the world, a perfect light in the Lord (sevenfold being a sign of perfection), and hears the voice of the heavenly Bridegroom: "Thou art all fair, my love; there is no spot in thee" (Song 4:7).

30.17.s.en: 4. The wrath of God against Assyria:

30.17.0.en: 27 Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, his anger kindled, and the burning great: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire: 28 And his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck, to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity: and there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err. 29 Ye shall have a song, as in the night when a holy solemnity is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come into the mountain of the LORD, to the mighty One of Israel. 30 And the LORD shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall shew the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a devouring fire, with scattering, and tempest, and hailstones. 31 For through the voice of the LORD shall the Assyrian be beaten down, which smote with a rod. 32 And in every place where the grounded staff shall pass, which the LORD shall lay upon him, it shall be with tabrets and harps: and in battles of shaking will he fight with it. 33 For Tophet is ordained of old; yea, for the king it is prepared; he hath made it deep and large: the pile thereof is fire and much wood; the breath of the LORD, like a stream of brimstone, doth kindle it.

30.17.1.en: Most scholars see that what is mentioned here is a description of the destruction that fell upon the army of Sennacherib, although Assyria with its army and its commander represents the powers of darkness that bear enmity against God under the leadership of the devil himself, who seeks to storm the Church of the Lord, our inner Jerusalem, in order to sit enthroned in the holy temple of our hearts.

30.17.2.en: A. "Behold, the name of the LORD cometh from far, his anger kindled, and the burning great: his lips are full of indignation, and his tongue as a devouring fire: and his breath, as an overflowing stream, shall reach to the midst of the neck" [27]. "Cometh from far" because He was long-suffering toward Assyria, in case it might turn back from the pride of its heart, and He waited long, for He does not seek punishment but the return of all to Him, and His name still comes from far, being long-suffering toward the wicked, that perhaps they may repent. As the Apostle Paul says: "Or despisest thou the riches of his goodness and forbearance and longsuffering; not knowing that the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance?" (Rom 5:4).

30.17.3.en: "The name of God" dwells in the life of the Church, is declared in the heart of the believer, is near to him, nearer than himself, but to the wicked it seems very far, and even sometimes he thinks it does not exist. This name is a strong tower for the believers (Ps 18:50) and a kindled anger and a great burning for those who resist.

30.17.4.en: The lips of the Lord drop fatness for His children and are full of indignation for those who deny Him!

30.17.5.en: His tongue calls all to His heavenly goods and is as a devouring fire to the disobedient.

30.17.6.en: His breath bestows comfort and a peace which passeth all understanding on the Church, for the Lord breathed on the face of His disciples and gave them His Holy Spirit working in them for the forgiveness of sins (Jn 20:22); but for those who reject the faith, His breath is as an overflowing stream that reaches to their neck.

30.18.0.en: He likens the nations to an empty harvest that is all straw without wheat, or to unruly horses that bridles do not restrain, for he says: "to sift the nations with the sieve of vanity (the sieve of nothingness)" [28], for they sift and the sieve brings up nothing. "And there shall be a bridle in the jaws of the people, causing them to err" [28]. Bridles are put in their mouths but they do not walk in the way of truth.

30.19.0.en: B. "Ye shall have a song, as in the night when a holy solemnity is kept; and gladness of heart, as when one goeth with a pipe to come into the mountain of the LORD, to the mighty One of Israel. And the LORD shall cause his glorious voice to be heard, and shall shew the lighting down of his arm, with the indignation of his anger, and with the flame of a devouring fire, with scattering, and tempest, and hailstones" [29-30].

30.19.1.en: The destruction of the enemy turns into joy for the people, as on a Paschal night... Perhaps what concerns the believers is not the destruction of the enemy (even the devil himself and his angels) but the removal of the obstacles so that they come to the mountain of the Lord, to heaven itself, rejoicing. Our goal is not to gloat over the enemy of good, but our enjoyment of the glory of the Lord and our hearing His voice.

30.20.0.en: C. Isaiah sees in the return of the people from captivity to Jerusalem something like a military procession entering its country with military music proclaiming victory; "And in every place where the grounded staff shall pass, which the LORD shall lay upon him, it shall be with tabrets and harps: and in battles of shaking will he fight with it" [32].

30.21.0.en: D. He presents a final picture of the extent of Assyria's destruction, for he depicts the place of the fire, "Tophet," the place where the remains were burned outside Jerusalem, as prepared to contain the king, "the god Moloch," who will burn with the wrath of the Lord [33].
